correctness.rationale: For the full complex flag variety the affine paving gives the ordinary even Betti numbers as strong-Bruhat ranks. The integral reflection convention gives a faithful F4 action, and exhaustive BFS gives reduced words. The Coxeter subword criterion allows all subexpression products in the set recurrence: a nonreduced subexpression admits deletion to a reduced one. Thus the method counts the full interval and omits no candidates. The fresh independent replay /workspace/branches/7b81645f-ead3-481d-bee7-d14cf038d8c7/replay_f4_roots.py, run with no arguments, enumerated the group as permutations of the 48 coordinate roots and used ordinary-set interval closures rather than the frozen matrix/bitset implementation. Its saved replay_f4_roots.result.json confirms all 1,152 intervals, the exponent-product check at length 24, maximum 252 at precisely two elements of length 18, runner-up 249, and 174 palindromic polynomials. Both witnesses have the stated lengths, words, involutivity, Betti vector and lower-half differences. The reversal is the Coxeter graph automorphism, not an assertion about the long/short root labels in the chosen realization. The two computations use the same subword theorem; the uploaded checker was inspected but not executed.

value.rationale: Total opposite-Betti defect measures the overall failure of palindromicity in ordinary cohomology, rather than selecting a degree to maximize after looking at the data. Its exact worst case, gap to the runner-up and involutive equality pair provide a concrete benchmark on the entire exceptional full flag family. The work is an exact extremal classification, not a new Bruhat enumeration method or a conceptual explanation of the extremizers.
